claim: A control harness (pre-solve feeling of knowing, post-solve judgment of learning, a fitted stop/retry rule, forced-choice selection) raised Claude Sonnet 4.6 pooled pass@1 from 48.3 to 56.9 (+8.6) on 1,859 questions at 2.4 attempts and $0.78 vs $0.29 per question. Size-weighted per-benchmark figures re-compute to the pooled numbers (checked in cross-check).
agent_test: Rebuild a stop/retry gate on our agent; compare against pass@1, plain best-of-K and majority vote at the same total tokens on a held-out set of at least 300 items with 3 seeds.

claim: The paper does not show a win at equal compute. The harness costs about 2.7x pass@1 and no arm uses plain best-of-2.4, majority vote or self-consistency at matched dollars. It beats the listed baselines at lower cost than the 4-attempt ones, but those are weak comparators. On LiveCodeBench the 4-attempt Aggregator (83.4 at $0.94) nearly matches the harness (84.3 at $0.56).
agent_test: Always include a matched-token best-of-K plus majority-vote arm in every comparison; report accuracy per 1,000 tokens.

claim: Gains are concentrated where the model reports low or medium first-attempt confidence (JOL band accuracy 0.16 to 0.42 and 0.36 to 0.55); high-confidence items do not gain (0.67 to 0.64). LiveCodeBench Hard gains +19.6 while Easy is flat (-0.7). Band sizes are not reported and bands are cut by the same signal that drives control, so regression to the mean may inflate the low band. Gap check: a second-pass gain in a band cut by the first pass's own confidence can be partly regression to the mean; no placebo re-ask arm has been shown (Cao or Illusion of Insight).
agent_test: Bin held-out items by first-attempt confidence on an independent split; compare retry vs no-retry within bins at matched tokens.

claim: The claim that a learned directed retry rule beats random retry at the same budget is not supported: 47.0 vs 45.7 on N=100 (CI about 20 points wide). The hand rule (1-JOL)xFOK and FOK-only scored 42.0, below pass@1 44.0, so the harness is fragile to controller choice. Gap check 2026-10-26: an independent matched-budget test with a different (text-feature) controller found directed beats random by 3 to 4 points on MATH N=200 (Zhai et al.), so directed allocation is plausible, but retry with feedback is still untested at N of 500 or more. Cao's random-retry CI [43,48] is far narrower than the other arms, so the comparison is not like for like.
agent_test: Run directed vs random retry at equal mean K on at least 500 items with a paired bootstrap on per-item differences.

claim: Independent 4-attempt sampling plus an aggregator scored 45.0 in the ablation, below the 2.58-attempt harness at 47.0 and near pass@1 44.0. This is the closest thing in the paper to an equal-compute comparator, and the gap is inside noise.
agent_test: Same comparison on our agent with 3 seeds, counting tokens not attempts.

claim: Showing later attempts only a compact record (prior answers, confidence scores, reasons) did better than showing full prior reasoning (47.0 vs 40.0); full-context retry fell below pass@1 (44.0). Authors argue anchoring on failed trajectories; the mechanism is not isolated. Counter-evidence: Sharma and Chopra (2025) found sequential chains that see full previous reasoning beat parallel chains in 43 of 45 matched-token configurations (4,096-token cap per step, single seed, open models); the cap may explain part of it.
agent_test: A/B retry context (compact summary vs full trace vs nothing) at equal tokens on items where the first attempt failed.

claim: Confidence is useful across problems but not within a problem: median within-problem JOL SD is 0.048 vs 0.270 across problems (5.6x), and max-JOL selection (44.0) gave no gain over pass@1 (44.0). Use confidence to decide whether to spend more, not to pick among attempts.
agent_test: Compare max-confidence selection with verifier or vote selection on the same candidate pools.

claim: Whether a model's confidence signals can drive control varies by model and can be checked on a small anchor set: Sonnet 4.6 FOK AUROC 0.612 (barely above the 0.60 bar), JOL 0.745, joint 0.757, joint ECE 0.087; Gemma 4 FOK AUROC 0.534 fails. The anchor set is N=100, so intervals are wide, and the controller was fitted on those same items.
agent_test: Measure our agent's pre-solve and post-solve confidence AUROC and ECE on at least 300 labelled items before trusting any gate.

claim: Verbalized confidence is weak in older models and much better when derived from agreement across samples: GPT-4 vanilla verbalized AUROC 62.7 (random is 50); GSM8K AUROC 54.8 vs 92.7 with 5-sample consistency. Cao's Sonnet 4.6 joint AUROC 0.757 suggests newer models are better, but models and tasks differ.
agent_test: Compare verbalized confidence against 3-sample agreement as the gate signal on our agent at the same tokens.

claim: Prompted intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not reliably help reasoning and often hurts in 2023-era models (GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1). Gains appear with an oracle or reliable external feedback. A replication on reasoning models is missing. Scope note 2026-10-26: this claim stays established for 2023-era instruction models only. For reasoning models see K23.
agent_test: Test same-model critique-and-revise vs tool-grounded check at equal tokens; keep revisions only when an external check endorses them.

claim: Multi-agent debate does not beat self-consistency at matched response counts. GSM8K GPT-3.5: debate round 1 (6 responses) 83.2 vs SC 85.3; round 2 (9 responses) 83.0 vs SC 88.2; SC with 3 responses 82.5.
agent_test: Accept a critique or debate step only if it beats majority vote at equal tokens.

claim: Self-bias grows over self-refinement rounds when the model scores its own output; larger models and accurate external feedback reduce it.
agent_test: Check whether our selector prefers its own earlier outputs; swap authorship labels and compare.

claim: Stopping sampling when answers agree saves compute at near-zero accuracy loss for strong models: early-stopping self-consistency cut samples 33.8% (MATH) to 84.2% (Coin Flip); GPT-4 accuracy change 0.00 on MATH, GSM8K, CSQA. Weaker models lose more (GPT-3.5 StrategyQA -0.19). Agreement among samples of one model is correlated.
agent_test: Add an agreement-based stop window to our retry loop; measure tokens saved and accuracy change.

claim: Compute should follow problem difficulty: easy items gain from sequential revision, medium and hard items from search, and the hardest items from no test-time method. Estimating difficulty has its own cost, which the original does not count.
agent_test: Route by first-pass confidence to one of three strategies; compare with a fixed strategy at equal total tokens.

claim: Reasoning models spend far more tokens than needed on easy problems (2+3: 1,953% more tokens; in over 92% of cases the first solution was already right); a self-training fix cut 48.6% of tokens on MATH500 at kept accuracy. The fix is training; a stop gate is the scaffold analogue.
agent_test: Measure the share of our agent's tokens spent after the first correct answer.

claim: Always-retrieve and always-multi-step pipelines waste compute; routing by question complexity matched multi-step quality at lower cost (Adaptive-RAG GPT-3.5 F1 50.91 vs 50.87, time 1.46 vs 3.33 units against 0.86 for single-step), but a large gap to the oracle router remains (62.80). Time units in the table are ambiguous.
agent_test: Trigger retrieval or tool calls by a cheap complexity or uncertainty gate; compare with always-on at equal cost.

claim: Monitoring skill and answering skill do not rank together across models: in 20 frontier LLMs (524 items) Claude Haiku 4.5 ranked 13th on accuracy but 2nd on withdraw sensitivity, GLM-5 1st on accuracy but 9th, Gemini 3.1 Pro 6th on accuracy and last on monitoring (-1.0). Sonnet 4.6 had the largest withdraw delta (+39.4). Single administration, no test-retest, Cronbach alpha 0.54.
agent_test: Measure our base model's own withdraw delta before deciding how much control to give its self-reports.

claim: Detecting a likely error does not mean acting on it: Sonnet 4.6 had the top retrospective withdraw delta yet chose to answer directly on 98.6% of exploratory T6 items. Correlation between retrospective and prospective measures was r=.17, CI [-.29,.57], n=20, underpowered. This supports putting control in code rather than trusting the model to act on its own doubt.
agent_test: Compare model-chosen abstain or hint requests with a code rule on the same confidence value at equal tokens.

claim: Metacognitive prompting (single-pass script: understand, judge, evaluate, decide, assess confidence) gives modest gains on language-understanding tasks, relative +4.8% to 6.4% over zero-shot CoT, with no code-level gate and no token-cost comparison.
agent_test: Add a prompt-only arm at equal tokens so gains over a plain careful prompt are separated from gate effects.

claim: Forced extra thinking (budget forcing) has diminishing returns and is not uncertainty-gated: s1-32B AIME24 50.0 to 53.3 with 2x Wait, up to 57 at best setting, flattening near 6x; AIME24 has 30 questions, so one item is 3.3 points. In Cao, budget forcing gave +3.2 pooled at $0.67.
agent_test: Cap extension count; compare ungated vs confidence-gated extension at equal tokens.

claim: Small-sample ablation gaps (1 to 5 points on N=100) should not be treated as findings; several arms of Cao's Table 2 fall below pass@1, so the design is fragile and is untested at scale or on agent tasks. No independent replication of the harness was found as of 2026-10-26 (arXiv lists v1 only, no code link; the two Semantic Scholar citers, a Yale survey and a Meta agentic paper, were read and neither is a replication).
agent_test: Pre-register ablations with N>=500 and paired tests; report failed arms.

claim: Self-written tests or self-assessed pass signals can mislead a gate: Reflexion fell on MBPP because self-generated tests gave false negatives, while its HumanEval gain (91 vs 80) relies on executable feedback.
agent_test: Audit the false-negative rate of our agent's self-generated checks before they gate retries.

claim: Reasoning-trained models do correct errors that sit in their own context, unlike non-reasoning models: the self-correction blind spot is 64.5% on average over 14 open non-reasoning models and near zero or negative in reasoning models, and appending 'Wait' cuts it by 89.3%. But spontaneous mid-trace pivots are rare and go with lower accuracy (6.31% of traces; 2.57% vs 16.44% correct), and prompted revision adds little for DeepSeek-R1-class models at its token price. No one has re-run the Huang review-your-answer protocol on Sonnet 4.6 or another 2026 frontier reasoning model.
agent_test: Run the Huang protocol (answer, then 'review and revise', no feedback) on our model, 500+ items, count right-to-wrong and wrong-to-right flips at equal tokens against a plain second sample.

claim: Allocating a fixed sample budget by disagreement among a few probe samples beats uniform self-consistency at the same total samples in small and mid open models, +2.5 average (9 of 15 cells significant by paired bootstrap, three seeds), and a learned allocator beats random allocation at the same mean cost by 3 to 4 points on MATH (N=200). The gain shrinks with budget and a simple early-stop rule is as good for the larger models. This is a far smaller effect than the harness headline.
agent_test: At equal total tokens compare uniform majority vote, adaptive stop on agreement, and the confidence harness, on 3 seeds with paired bootstrap.

claim: For black-box reasoning models, a single verbalized confidence is a decent signal (math AUROC 71.3) and self-consistency alone is weaker at small K; one verbalized confidence plus agreement of two samples reaches 84.2 in math and beats either signal at K=8. Agreement alone is not safe: a more confident model can have agreement that is uncorrelated or negatively correlated with correctness (gpt-4.1 on GPQA: 48% wrong at agreement 0.8 or more).
agent_test: On our model, compare JOL alone, 2-sample agreement alone, JOL plus agreement, and a verifier as stop signals, at equal tokens, on AUROC and on end-to-end accuracy per token.

claim: Raw verbalized confidence from open reasoning models is not good enough to drive control without recalibration: mean ECE 0.268 and AUROC 0.635 over 36 model-dataset pairs, against Cao's bar of ECE below 0.15 and AUROC at least 0.6. Cao's Sonnet 4.6 numbers (JOL AUROC 0.745, FOK 0.612) are model-specific; ECE alone can pass a near-uninformative signal (Gemma 4 joint ECE 0.044 with FOK AUROC 0.534).
agent_test: Gate on a bootstrap lower bound of AUROC above 0.6 and ECE below 0.15, together, using at least a few hundred labelled items; do not accept ECE alone.

claim: A controller-plus-workers harness with compact state beat a flat-history 'direct control' agent at the same nominal model-call budget in all 12 matched agent comparisons (for example ProgramBench GPT-5.5 71.5 vs 63.7), but loses at small budgets (Opus 4.8 at 400 calls: 56.6 vs 62.7). Calls are matched, not tokens or cost; the direct agent uses only about 18% of its allowance; no component is isolated. It is not a replication of Cao and does not use FOK or JOL.
agent_test: In agent tasks, charge the controller's own tokens to the same budget and report the break-even budget where control starts to pay.

claim: When errors have explicit costs, models do not hold a stable act-or-escalate stance: implicit thresholds vary from 53% to 91% accuracy within one model family and are not predicted by scale, and in an agent benchmark abstention is largely independent of solving ability (best of 17 models 59.5% paired accuracy) with abstention often coming after an irreversible step. Supports a code-level cost threshold placed before irreversible actions.
agent_test: Measure our agent's implicit escalation threshold on paired act/abstain tasks; set the threshold in code from labelled cost ratios.

claim: Open question left by new evidence: directed (confidence-gated) retry has not been compared with plain best-of-K plus majority vote at matched tokens on a 2026 frontier model with seeds and paired tests, and its stop-decision and extra-attempt effects have not been separated. Every adjacent matched-budget test found smaller gains (+1.5 to +4) than the +8.6 headline.
agent_test: Factorial design: stop gate on/off x retry-with-compact-history on/off x selector on/off, plus plain best-of-K and majority vote at the measured token total, 3 seeds, N at least 500 per benchmark.
